summary: The team is juggling an urgent Outlook account lockout, the launch of the Intelligent China webpage, and final touches on video and newsletter content, while advancing the knowledge website redesign and global marketing strategy.
summaryDetail: Right now, the most pressing issue is the Outlook account lockout: everyone must delete and re-login to all email accounts, check home devices, and contact JSB to confirm backend unlock status. In parallel, the Intelligent China webpage is set to launch this week to start driving traffic, as part of the broader push to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China for SEO and marketing, with US programs (including Berkeley as a possible third priority) on hold. This week also sees critical content deadlines: Joseph must share final videos today (after fixing sync and title issues) and schedule the September newsletter, while Ira and Kaylee discuss the 2026 WIL Forum agenda and Kaylee has a call with Wenjuan Zhou on Tuesday. The knowledge website redesign is moving forward with Joseph sharing the inspiration HTML and a half-hour feedback session before Joker implements changes, and the global marketing strategy needs Joseph to draft target areas and the team to audit conversion tracking. Looking ahead, the Li Wei article translation needs confirmation, the Custom Program page copy requires accuracy checks, and the WIL Forum planning continues to develop.

meetings.summary: The team reviewed the knowledge website redesign, comparing the current version with Joseph's inspiration layout. They agreed the menu categorization is improved but the overall design is too similar to the existing site, and discussed incorporating more articles and indices while removing the outdated video section.

meetings.title: CKGSB Global Marketing Strategy Meeting
meetings.summary: The team discussed prioritizing China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) for SEO and marketing, with a focus on understanding target audience and conversion tracking. They agreed to draft a strategy, audit existing tracking, and consider US programs as secondary.
